findings-against-prior-runs.finding: The prior runs concluded exit 23 (SettingsServerError) 'is not cheaply arrangeable live in this build' because 'an explicit non-default port always auto-starts a working backend rather than erroring' when pointed at an unbound port, and substituted a unit test instead. This is not actually a limit of the build -- it is a limitation of the specific probe they tried. Reading src/AiRaccoon/Hosting/Common/ServerProbe.cs shows BackendLauncher.AcquireAsync only self-launches a backend when the port gives NO answer to a POST /mcp probe; if something answers with a status outside the transient set (5xx/408/429) and a body containing the literal string 'jsonrpc', ServerProbe reports ProbeVerdict.Answered and BackendLauncher attaches to it instead of spawning anything. A ~50-line fake HTTP server satisfying that contract (400 + 'jsonrpc' body on /mcp, 500 on /settings*), paired with a copied mcp-token file in the scratch data root (McpTokenFile.Read() only requires the right base64url length, not a server-minted value), reliably drives a live settings command to exit 23 -- verified in this run against the real installed 1.33.0 binary. The item's own suggested method ('point at a dead port') was correctly found not to work; the conclusion that 23 therefore cannot be driven live at all does not follow, and was reused unmodified across two consecutive runs. Review follow-up: ServerProbe.cs's own doc comment claims a {400,401,405,406} status gate the code does not implement (any non-transient status with a 'jsonrpc' body is Answered) -- the stale comment is what the prior runs' belief rested on; filed as #539.

Five consecutive runs marked this item 'substituted' with the reason that "the '#section' query form does not exist as syntax" and verified chunk resolution via chunkIndex/totalChunks instead. The syntax exists: src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Sqlite/Memory/SourcePathQuery.cs (ADR-0003) rewrites a query matching ^[\w./-]+\.(md|markdown|txt)(#[\w-]+)?$ into an FTS {source_file section} column query with AND semantics, and this run observed it live ('manual.md#no-such-section' -> 0 results with the vector leg off, while the same words in keyword shape -> 2). The runs could not see it because a default hybrid search always returns vector-leg hits, so the anchor's answer was indistinguishable from a keyword coincidence -- the item needs vectorWeight=0 to be able to fail. The substitution hid a real defect (#538, the #489 residual) for five releases; this is the 'plausible-sounding reason that is right about the outcome and wrong about the cause' the skill warns about.
